definition: A key concept in object-oriented programming in which a unit's inner workings are hidden from users and other units that do not need to know them.
The practice of assigning an alternative name to an imported item, such as a module, within a program. It is commonly used to prevent name collisions.
A logical operator that takes multiple condition operands and evaluates to True or False.
An operation used to add an element to the end of a list.
A symbol used to perform mathematical calculations such as addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.
The American Standard Code for Information Interchange, a character encoding system originally defining 128 code points to support the English language.
The single = character used in a statement to store a value into a variable. It assigns the value on its right side to the variable on its left side, distinct from the equal sign in mathematics.
A statement that sets a variable to a value using the assignment operator (=). The variable name is placed on the left side, and the value to be assigned is on the right side.

The rule that determines the order of operations when adjacent operators share the same level of precedence. Operations can be evaluated from left to right (left associative) or from right to left (right associative).
A specific input value in a recursive algorithm for which the solution is already known. It stops the recursion to prevent infinite computation.
A format used by computers to store information as strings of only two allowed values, 0 and 1.
A recursive algorithm used to efficiently search sorted lists by checking the middle element and discarding about half the items at each step.
A data type that represents a binary value of either true or false.
A binary value that is either true or false. In Python, it belongs to the bool data type and is represented by the capitalized keywords True and False.
A variable that is assigned a value of either True or False.
A visualization used to display the distribution of a continuous variable, highlighting its minimum, maximum, quartiles, and outliers.
A group of statements that execute based on a condition.
A statement used within a for or while loop that immediately terminates the loop and moves program execution past it once a specific condition is met.
A standard library function that is always available in Python without needing to be imported.
A blueprint that defines the fields and procedures used to model objects and create instances. It can store shared class attributes that belong to the class itself rather than individual instances.
An attribute that belongs to a class itself and is shared across all instances of that class, accessed using the format class_name.attribute_name.
A unique numeric value assigned to represent a specific character within an encoding standard like ASCII or Unicode.
A text-based file format used to store structured data where entries and fields are typically separated by commas.
A short phrase that explains what code is doing, beginning with a hash character (#). All text from the hash character to the end of the line is ignored when running the program.
An operator used to compare values, yielding a Boolean result of either true or false.
A relationship between classes where one class contains an instance of another class. It represents a 'has-a' relationship.
An electronic device that stores and processes information.
A sequence of statements that run one after the other.
An operation that combines two or more strings sequentially using the concatenation operator (+). It joins strings directly without inserting default separator characters such as spaces.
An expression that evaluates to true or false, used to determine whether a body of statements in a decision-making structure will execute.
A simplified, single-line version of an if-else statement that checks a condition and evaluates one of two expressions depending on whether that condition is true or false.
An object that can hold an arbitrary number of other objects.
A statement used in a loop that skips the remainder of the current iteration without exiting the loop entirely, allowing the loop expression to be evaluated again.
The sequence in which a program executes its instructions. It starts at the main program and can skip or jump to different lines rather than following a strictly linear path.
A method that counts the number of occurrences of a substring within a given string, returning 0 if the substring does not exist.
The process of selecting rows or columns from a dataset based on specified conditions.
A multidisciplinary field that combines collecting, processing, and analyzing large volumes of data to extract insights and drive informed decision-making.

An iterative framework followed by data scientists to complete a data science project. It progresses through stages including data acquisition, data exploration, and data analysis to generate insights or predictive models.
The process of selecting a specific subset of rows and/or columns from a DataFrame using ranges, lists, or Boolean conditions.
The format a programming language uses to represent data.
A Pandas data structure that organizes data into columns with specified column names and data types. It can be instantiated from sources such as a dictionary, list, NumPy array, or CSV file.
A predefined value assigned to a function parameter that is automatically used if a positional or keyword argument is not supplied during a function call.
An arrangement of elements in a sequence from largest to smallest.
An issue that arises in multiple inheritance when a class inherits from multiple classes that share a common superclass.
A container object in Python that stores key-value pairs and does not allow duplicate keys.
A concise and efficient way to create a dictionary by transforming elements of an iterable object into key-value pairs using curly braces.

A string, usually written across multiple lines, that provides documentation for people who use a program without necessarily reading its source code. It typically consists of a one-line summary, a blank line, and a longer description.
A Python variable that begins and ends with double underscores and possesses a special meaning within the language.

A statement (short for "else if") that checks a condition only when the preceding decision statement's condition is false. It is used to chain multiple conditions together within a complex decision structure.
A statement paired with an if statement that contains a body of actions to be executed when the if statement's condition is false.

A key concept in object-oriented programming that involves bundling data and the procedures that operate on that data into a single unit while restricting external access to prevent direct modification.
A combination of characters starting with a backslash that represents a special character within a string.
A technique for finding the greatest common divisor (GCD) by recursively subtracting the smaller integer from the larger integer until both integers are equal.
A section of code that runs in response to an exception raised in a try statement, allowing a program to handle errors and continue executing rather than terminating.
The intentional conversion of a value from one data type to another performed by a programmer to enable a specific operation.
The process of visually and statistically examining data to gain insights, identify patterns, understand underlying structures, and assess data quality.
A piece of code that represents a single value to be computed. It can range from a single value or literal to an arbitrarily long combination of literals, variables, and operators.
The product of a positive integer and all the positive integers less than that integer.
An individual variable or attribute calculated from the raw data in a dataset.
A sequence of numbers in which each number is the sum of the previous two numbers in the sequence, commonly beginning with 0 and 1 or two 1s.
The minimum length specified for a string within a string format specification. If the string value is shorter than this minimum, it is padded with space characters.
A temporary storage area where data is automatically held when using the write() function before being finalized and saved to a file.
A string method that returns the index of the first occurrence of a substring in a given string, or -1 if the substring does not exist.
A basic numerical data type used to represent decimal numbers.
An iterative loop designed to access objects one at a time by iterating over all elements in a container. It is commonly used for both iteration and counting.
A directive inside an f-string replacement field, introduced by a colon, that defines how a value should be formatted for display.

A string literal prefixed with 'f' or 'F' that can contain replacement fields in curly braces ({}) to evaluate and insert expressions into the text. It provides a convenient way to combine multiple values into one string.
A named, reusable block of code that performs a task when called. It is defined using the def keyword followed by the function name, parentheses, a colon, and an indented body of statements.
A value passed as input to a function during a function call.
A programming language feature that allows multiple functions to share the same name if their parameters are different.
A variable in a function definition that represents the input received by the function.
The region of a program in which a variable created outside of a function—or declared using the global keyword—can be accessed anywhere during the entire program execution.
A Google document containing executable cells that can be run, created, and modified, and shared with other Google accounts to report and share insights.
A comparison operator that evaluates two values and returns True if the left value is strictly greater than the right value, and False otherwise.
A comparison operation that compares two values and evaluates to True if the left value is greater than or equal to the right value, and False otherwise.
An integer that serves as a divisor for both of two given positive integers.
A connection between classes where one class contains an instance of another class rather than inheriting from it. This relationship is also referred to as composition.
A built-in Python function that provides a summary of a module's functions and data based on its docstrings.
A type of inheritance where multiple subclasses inherit directly from a single superclass.
A programming language with source code designed for humans to understand rather than computers. Programs written in these languages must be translated into low-level machine code to run.
A type of plot used to show the distribution or trend of continuous variables.
A language used to design websites and graphical applications that web browsers read and render. It defines standard color names and supports color specifications using hexadecimal RGB values.
An integer representing the memory location of an object. Along with type and value, it is one of the fundamental characteristics of every object.
A decision-making structure that contains a condition and a body of statements. The body is executed if the condition is true and skipped if the condition is false.
A property of an object indicating that its contents cannot be modified or altered once it has been created. Any desired changes require creating a new object, leaving the original unchanged.
An object that cannot be modified after it is created. When passed into a function, any modifications require making a local copy, meaning changes do not persist outside the function.
An automatic process where the Python interpreter converts one data type to another without requiring the programmer to specify the conversion.
A statement that defines a variable used to access code contained within a module. It typically appears at the beginning of a program.
An operator used to test if one string contains another by returning True or False, or to iterate through the individual characters of a string in a for loop.

A number that refers to the specific position of a character in a string or an element in a list. Indexes start at 0 from left to right (ending at one less than the sequence's length) or start at -1 from right to left.
A loop that does not have a termination condition and continues executing indefinitely unless stopped.

An is-a relationship in object-oriented programming where a subclass inherits all attributes and methods from a superclass and extends its functionality. It allows classes to reuse existing code without redefining everything, reducing redundancy and promoting modularity.
Data or information that a user enters into a computer program.
An individual object created from a class blueprint that possesses its own specific attributes and methods.
A variable that is unique to each instance of a class and is accessed using the format instance_name.attribute_name.
A method defined within a class that is used to access and modify both instance attributes and class attributes.
A basic number format and data type that represents a whole number.
A programming language in which source code is translated into machine code and executed one line at a time while the program is running.

A program that translates high-level source code into machine code and executes it one line at a time while the program is running. It halts translation and displays an error message if an error occurs.
A relationship between a subclass and a superclass in which the subclass inherits all attributes and methods from the superclass and extends its functionality.
A string method that concatenates a list of string elements into a single output string, inserting a specified delimiter between each element.
The first item in a dictionary's key-value pair, analogous to a word listed with its definition in a language dictionary.
A reserved word in Python that serves a special function and cannot be used as a name for a variable or other object.
An argument that uses a parameter name to assign a value rather than relying on order.
A comparison operator that evaluates two values, returning True if the first value is smaller than the second and False otherwise.
A comparison operation that evaluates two values, returning True if the first value is less than or equal to the second value, and False otherwise.
A collection of code that can be used in other programs.
An object used to bundle elements together in Python, defined using square brackets containing comma-separated values. It can contain elements of any single type or a combination of different types.
A Python statement used to compactly create a new list using a pattern, with the optional ability to filter items using conditions.
A larger list in which every element is itself a smaller list, commonly used to represent multidimensional data.
The scope of a variable created within a function, meaning it exists only while the function is executing and cannot be accessed from outside that function.
An operator that takes one or more condition operands and evaluates them to produce a value of True or False.
A code block that executes a set of statements repeatedly while a given condition is true. It is often used to perform repetitive tasks or iterate over elements in a list.
The set of statements executed repeatedly inside a loop construct as long as the loop condition remains true.
A block of code that executes after a loop completes normally, without being interrupted by a break statement.
The condition in a while loop that is evaluated at each iteration to determine whether the loop body should continue executing.
A Python string method that returns the alphabetical characters of a string converted to lowercase without modifying the original string.
A funny story constructed using words provided by a user.
A special method that begins and ends with double underscores to perform actions typically out of the user's view. Programmers can define magic methods within a class to customize specific behaviors.
A built-in function that takes a list and returns its largest element, provided the elements in the list are comparable.
A visual representation that shows the relationship between variables and the objects they refer to in memory.
The practice of a subclass defining a method with the same name as a superclass method to change or replace inherited functionality.
A function that takes a list as a parameter and returns the smallest element in that list, provided its elements are comparable.
A class used in multiple inheritance that promotes modularity and helps eliminate the diamond problem.
A setting passed to the open() function that specifies whether a file is opened for reading only or for writing.
Previously written Python code stored in a .py file that can be imported and used in another program.
The unit or amount by which a value is divided in division and modulo operations.
A type of inheritance in which a subclass becomes the superclass for another class.
A type of inheritance in which a single class inherits from multiple superclasses, which are listed in the class definition's inheritance list.
A data type whose content can be modified after creation, allowing items to be added, updated, or deleted.
An object that can be modified after it is created. When a mutable object is passed into a function and modified, those changes persist outside the function.
A built-in variable that holds the name of a module when imported, or evaluates to "__main__" if the module is run directly as a program.

A situation that occurs when a function is defined multiple times, such as when different modules share the same function name. When this happens, Python uses the most recent definition without raising an error, which can lead to unexpected behavior.
An error that occurs when a variable name cannot be found, which may result from a missing import statement.

A replacement field in a string template that is tagged with a label or name key instead of relying on positional ordering. It improves code readability and can be used more than once in the template.
A NumPy data type and multi-dimensional array structure that stores homogeneous numeric data across any number of dimensions for efficient processing.
A method of referencing characters in a string from right to left using negative integers, where the right-most character has an index of -1 and the left-most character has an index of -len(s).
A dictionary that is stored as a value inside another dictionary.
A list that exists as an element inside another, larger list, often used to represent multidimensional data.
A loop construct that contains one or more loops within the body of another loop, where the outer loop controls how many times the inner loop fully executes.
The placement of a decision statement inside another decision statement, indicated in code by an indentation level.
A character that directs the display to move to the next line. It is added to the end of output by default when using the print() function.
An operator that takes a single condition operand, returning True when the operand is false and False when the operand is true.
A placeholder in a string that uses zero-based numerical indices to insert values based on the positional ordering of arguments provided to the format() method.
A Python library that provides support for efficient numerical operations on large, multi-dimensional arrays and serves as a fundamental building block for data analysis.
A single unit of data in a Python program.
A style of programming that groups related data members and procedures into objects, allowing real-world entities to be modeled as interacting components.
Customizing the function of a built-in operator, such as an arithmetic or comparison operator, to work with instances of user-defined classes.
A logical operator that takes two condition operands and evaluates to True if either condition is true.
The information or result produced by a program and displayed to the user.
An error that occurs when a value is too large to be stored, exceeding the maximum representable limit of floating-point numbers.
A word that is spelled the same forward and backward.
An open-source Python library used for data cleaning, processing, and analysis. It provides specialized data structures and tools to explore, manipulate, and analyze structured data efficiently.
Multidimensional structured datasets.
A statement used in Python as a placeholder to indicate that code will be written later, preventing errors that would happen if no code was written or if only a comment was used.
A unique identifier for a folder location on a computer. It is used along with a filename to access and open files stored in folders other than the one where the Python program exists.
The official style guide for Python that documents best practices for writing and formatting code.
A Python data visualization library used to create interactive visualizations across different plot types.

The concept where a single name is used for multiple functionalities. It allows different methods or operations sharing the same name to execute behavior determined by the calling object's class type.
An operation that removes the last item or element from a list without requiring any parameters.
An argument in a function call that is assigned to a parameter based on its sequential order. When mixed with keyword arguments, positional arguments must always be placed first.
The priority level of operators that determines which operation is evaluated first in an expression with multiple operators.
A number that is not divisible by any positive number larger than 1.
A sequence of instructions that a computer can run to accomplish tasks, create technology, and solve problems.
A document written by members of the Python community to propose new features or establish best practices and guidelines for the language.
The official third-party software library for Python where developers can share, install, and update modules.
A collection of over 200 built-in modules, functions, and types included with Python to support common programming tasks.
A free online tool used to visualize the line-by-line execution of Python code and draw memory diagrams.
A function that generates a sequence of integers between two numbers given a step size, which is inclusive of the start value and exclusive of the end value. It can take up to three input values.

A problem-solving technique that uses the solution to a simpler version of a problem to solve a larger problem. The process repeatedly applies this method to increasingly smaller subproblems until a solution is known or easily found, from which the larger solution is systematically built.
A structure used to trace and show the sequence of calls made by a recursive function and how the final values are computed.
A condition or input value for which recursion applies, causing a function to call itself with a smaller portion of the input parameter.
An action that removes a specified element from a list by passing that element as a parameter.
An operator that accepts a string operand and an integer operand to produce a repeated sequence of the string.
An acronym for 'read-eval-print loop' that is often used to refer to a shell, describing its repetitive nature.
A placeholder in a string template used to define a pattern for creating formatted string values. It can be populated using positional numbers or named labels.
A statement that ends a function's execution, transfers control flow back to the calling code, and can specify a value to send back to the caller.
The difference between an approximation of a value used in computation and the correct, true value, which occurs when floating-point values are stored erroneously as approximations.

The part of a program where a variable can be accessed. A variable's scope determines where it exists and whether it is accessible globally across the entire program or locally only within a specific function.
A reference to the specific instance of a class that called a method. It is used within class methods to access and initialize that instance's attributes.
A Pandas data structure that represents one-dimensional labeled data.
A program that allows direct, interactive communication with an interpreter to run code one line at a time.
An encryption technique in which each letter of a private message is replaced by another letter shifted by a set amount in the alphabet.
A naming convention that uses only lowercase letters and separates each word with an underscore.
The task of arranging elements in a sequence in ascending or descending order.
A string method that breaks a string into a list of substrings using a specified delimiter, or blank space characters if no argument is provided.
An instruction in a program that describes an action to be carried out. Programs consist of statements that are run sequentially one after the other.
The amount by which a counter variable's value changes during each iteration of a loop. It can be any positive or negative number to count in ascending or descending order.
A type of sequence made up of characters indexed from left to right, starting at index 0 and ending at index len(s) - 1.
The number of characters contained within a string object.
An operation that accesses a sequence of characters from a string using index boundaries. It returns characters starting from index a (inclusive) up to index b (exclusive).
A built-in function that takes a list of numbers and returns the sum of all elements in that list.
The rules that define how code must be structured in a programming language. It establishes the keywords, symbols, and formatting required to write valid programs.
A Python report indicating the location and type of an error. It prompts the programmer to trace back through the code to locate the issue if it is not immediately visible where Python flagged it.
An operator that converts an m by n array into an n by m array by transposing its dimensions.
A statement that runs code that might raise an exception, allowing a program to handle errors rather than terminate.

An ordered, immutable sequence of comma-separated values that can contain elements of different types and allows duplicates. Elements are accessed by index starting at 0, and the values are conventionally enclosed in parentheses.

The international standard for representing text on computers by assigning a unique number, called a code point, to each possible character. It extends ASCII to define over one million code points, supporting most of the world's written languages.
A string method that returns a string with all alphabetical characters converted to uppercase, leaving the original string unmodified.
The second item in a key-value pair stored inside a dictionary, associated with a corresponding key.
A named reference that allows a program to refer to and work with a value rather than directly using a memory location.
A code construct that repeatedly executes a set of statements, called the loop body, as long as a specified condition, known as the loop expression, remains true.
